entry_points: src/stringmol.cpp main (getopt -h; argv[1] = integer trial type dispatched by switch: 0 SmPm_1on1, 1 SmPm_AlifeXII, 2 SmPm_conpop, 3 origlife, 4 comass_GA, 5 joinsplists, 7 swdist, 8 comass_AlifeXII, 9 speigmonst, 30 run_stringmol_spatial, 34/35/36 spatial analysis, 44 comass_GA_boostwinners)
src/setupSM.cpp SmPm_AlifeXII (the 'grand-daddy' well-mixed container run: loads .conf, loops NTRIALS trials, each calling stringPM::TimestepIncrement per step and writing popdy/species/epoch files)

src/stringPM.cpp stringPM::TimestepIncrement (one timestep: repeatedly pick a random agent from the 'now' list, attempt decay, then if energy>0 either ReactionAttemptBind (unbound) or ReactionExecuteOpcode (bound pair), append to 'next' list)

src/stringPM.cpp stringPM::ReactionAttemptBind (picks a random unbound partner, aligns the two strings with AgentsAlign/Smith-Waterman, binds with probability bprob, sets active/passive roles, energy--)
src/stringPM.cpp stringPM::ReactionExecuteOpcode (switch on current opcode char: $ search, > move, = copy (mutation), + inc read, ^ toggle, ? if-label, % cleave, } terminate; default no-op)
src/opcodes.cpp OpcodeCopy (copy with indel/substitution mutation at indelrate/subrate when domut) and OpcodeCleave / OpcodeTerminate (product release, species registration in SMspp)
src/alignment.cpp SmithWaterman / SmithWatermanAlignment / ReactionCalculateBindProbability (string alignment against a substitution table .mtx to decide binding)
src/sm_spatial.cpp Stringmol_Spatial::Run (spatial variant on a GRIDX x GRIDY toroidal grid; loop while timestep<nsteps and molecules>0, saving PNG grids every IMAGEEVERY)

built_to: An 'Automata Chemistry': simulate containers (well-mixed, or spatial grids) of string molecules that bind by sequence alignment and execute each other as micro-programs (copy, cleave, search, move, toggle, if) so that replicase strings reproduce with mutation, and study the resulting species/population dynamics.
pressure: NOT_FOUND_AT_PIN (README gives no motivation statement; src/DEVNOTES.md lists past themes: 'Particle metabolome', 'molecular microprograms', 'Diversity from a monoculture', 'reaction logic', 'Degeneracy enriches', 'conservation of matter', 'maximize adjacent possible', 'extinction in replicase models')
success_means: NOT_FOUND_AT_PIN in README as a metric; the code records per-step molecule counts, species lists (SMspp), epochs and ancestry; README 'Issues' section lists repeatability, logging, zero-percent binds and SOFT_SEARCH as open problems
main_loop_one_sentence: Each timestep (stringPM::TimestepIncrement) drains the 'now' agent list by picking molecules at random, applying decay at decayrate, and -- while energy remains -- either trying to bind an unbound molecule to a random unbound partner with probability from a Smith-Waterman alignment against the substitution matrix (setting one as active executor and one as passive), or executing the active molecule's current opcode on the pair (search, move, copy-with-mutation, increment, toggle, if-label, cleave which releases a product into the population, or terminate), each executed step costing one unit of energy, then moving the molecules to the 'next' list which becomes 'now' for the following step.
behavioral_entry_point: src/stringPM.cpp:stringPM::ReactionExecuteOpcode (opcode semantics) and src/opcodes.cpp:OpcodeCopy (mutation rates indelrate/subrate); binding in src/stringPM.cpp:stringPM::ReactionAttemptBind + src/alignment.cpp:ReactionCalculateBindProbability; instruction/substitution table in config/*.mtx and src/alignment.cpp:default_table
lineage_notes: README: 'brief instructions to install, compile and run stringmol version 0.2.2' and 'url https://github.com/franticspider/stringmol.git' (a different GitHub owner than the pinned uoy-research repo). src/DEVNOTES.md: 'It begain in the Plazzmid project ... 2 years further work during EvoEvo'; flavours 'Vanilla' (papers before 2016), 'RUTSAC' (with Adam Nellis for the stringmol web app), 'Spatial' (with Paulien Hogeweg for R-P evolution, actively under development), 'FPGA' (Matthew Rowlings/Martin Trezfer, external), 'RStringmol' (external). Trial type 1 'ALife XII' is called 'the grand-daddy stringmol program'. CGI.md describes a web API (bind/step/bucket) from Adam Nellis. Headers on microbial_ga.* credit Verena Fischer.
